articles.title: Mission set to blast off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon
articles.summary: The spacecraft will head to Mars's larger moon, Phobos [JAXA] A spacecraft has launched from Japan headed for Mars' moon Phobos, where it will attempt to grab some moondust and bring it back to Earth. If it is successful, this will become the first time a sample has been returned from Mars or its moons to be analysed in laboratories here on Earth. The spacecraft is scheduled to arrive at Phobos in August 2027. It is hoped that the Mars Moons Exploration (MMX) mission, which is led by the Japanese Space Agency, will solve the mystery of how Mars's moons formed. Prof Sara Russell, from the Natural History Museum, who is the MMX mission's deputy for sample analysis, said: "There hasn't yet been a successful mission to go to Phobos and bring a bit back to Earth. "I think this is an incredibly ambitious and fun mission," she said. [BBC] There are only three moons in the inner Solar System: our own Moon, and two around Mars, which are called Phobos and Deimos. Both of these are tiny - Phobos is about 20km (12 miles) across and Deimos is about 10km (six miles) across. They are also irregularly shaped, looking a bit like space potatoes. The MMX spacecraft will study Deimos as it arrives in the Mars neighbourhood, and then will focus on Phobos. It plans to set down a small rover to explore the terrain, though this will be no easy feat. Sara Russell says no one has ever landed a rover on such a small moon. "The moon itself doesn't have very much of its own gravity," she explained. "But it's next to an enormous planet that's got a much higher gravity,  and that makes it much harder to get a rover onto the surface." Mars got its moons about 4.5bn years ago - but no one knows how they formed [NASA] The rover will scout out a landing site so that the MMX spacecraft itself can later touch down on Phobos. Once on the surface, it will deploy a robotic arm and two samplers to grab some moon dust. This material will be packed into a small capsule that will return to Earth in 2031, landing in the Woomera desert of South Australia. The amount of material that will come back is tiny - just 10g. "It's a very small [amount] actually," said Dr Chrysa Avdellidou, from Leicester University, who is working with the Japanese mission. "However we can do several studies even on individual grains… You don't need to have kilos back from a surface in order to do science.  So it's worth every gram," she said. The spacecraft will collect 10g of moon dust from the surface of Phobos [JAXA] Scientists believe the sample will finally shed light on the puzzle of where Mars's moons came from. There are two competing ideas. Either a space rock smashed into Mars early in its history, and Phobos and Deimos were created from the debris. Or the moons are two wandering asteroids from the outer Solar System, which were grabbed by the Red Planet's gravity. "When we get the sample back, we'll be able to look in detail at its chemistry and its mineral composition - and the two hypotheses will produce very distinct results," said Sara Russell. "It should be pretty much immediately obvious.. whether it's the product of this dramatic impact or whether it's a captured asteroid. So we'll find that out really quickly." The team is also hoping there might be an extra bonus coming back to their labs. "One of the really exciting things is that Phobos is so close to the Mars surface that whenever there's an impact into the Mars surface, little grains might actually become implanted into Phobos itself," said Russell. "And that means that the sample we get back may actually contain grains of Mars as well. So it can give us really direct information about the composition and history of Mars." Martian meteorites are rare - this one is on display at the Natural History Museum   [Kevin Church/BBC News] Bringing material from Mars back to Earth has long been an ambition of space scientists. The Nasa Perseverance rover, which has been exploring Mars since 2021, has been carefully collecting samples on Mars and storing them in canisters. But a second Nasa/ESA mission, called Mars Sample Return, that would have picked up and returned these canisters, has been effectively cancelled, after its funding was halted by the US Congress. China is planning its own sampling mission to Mars, set to launch in 2028. It will attempt to return Martian material to Earth in 2031. We do already have some fragments of the Red Planet here on Earth in the form of Martian meteorites. These are pieces of Mars that were blasted off the surface by asteroid strikes, and ended up being hurled towards the Earth. Martian meteorites are extremely rare, but like all space rocks that fall to our planet, they become contaminated as soon as they get here, mixing with the air, dust, soil and water. Scientists are so desperate to get their gloved hands on a direct sample from Mars and its moons because it would be pristine. articles.title: France imposes curfews after violent protests lead to thousands of arrests
articles.summary: By Sudip Kar-Gupta and Elizabeth Pineau PARIS, Oct 19 (Reuters) - French authorities set curfews in parts of several cities on Monday, including Paris, Lille and Nice, as they faced pressure over security failings after a weekend of riots and looting stemming from nationwide anti-government protests. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu had ruled out a blanket curfew in Paris but not a state of emergency, and had said ‌it was more appropriate for now to apply partial and localised curfews. "My determination to restore order is absolute," he told reporters. Paris police said they had issued orders barring protests in certain areas of ‌the French capital from 8 p.m. (1800 GMT) and had issued a curfew around the Place de la Republique and Les Halles from 11:00 p.m. Both would remain in effect until 6 a.m. on Tuesday morning. "A police deployment is in place to ensure strict compliance with these measures," ​the police said in a statement. A source in Lecornu's office said a curfew for minors had been set between 8 p.m. and 6 a.m. for the next two days in Lille, Douai, Wattignies and Denain with the agreement of the local mayors. In Nice, mayor Eric Ciotti said in a video posted online that he had signed an order installing a curfew for minors in central Nice overnight. Marseille banned gatherings and demonstrations. French unions meanwhile called for a new round of strikes and rallies on November 5. The weekend of looting and violence between some protesters and police followed weeks of student demonstrations, rocking France six months ahead of its next presidential election and highlighting pressures from a weak economy and surging debt. MINISTER ‌BLAMES FAR LEFT Lecornu blamed far-left groups for some of France's worst unrest in ⁠years. "There is, after all, a far-left movement that wants to cause — we can’t put it any more strongly — profound unrest in the country in the run-up to the presidential election," he said. Hard-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon urged him to provide evidence. "Otherwise, he should apologise, keep quiet and stop fanning the flames of unrest," he said on X. The Federation of Trade ⁠and Retail said almost 3,000 shops had been affected over the weekend. "Behind every ransacked shop are business owners, employees and families who have seen years of work and effort wiped out in a matter of hours," it added, calling for social security and tax relief for affected businesses. Lecornu said the government would provide furlough measures from Tuesday. Standing before a boarded-up shopfront, Gerard Nouchi, manager of two clothing stores in Marseille, said there weren't enough police to stop the looters. "They trashed everything, broke things, insulted ​us,” ​Nouchi said. "It was like a real tornado." The government ordered platforms selling looted goods to take down announcements and collaborate to prosecute ​resellers, Junior Digital Minister Anne Le Hénanff wrote on X. Some 2,400 people were arrested and ‌one protester died from a cardiac arrest on Saturday while nearly 1,000 officers were injured, according to the Interior Ministry. 'LEFT WITHOUT PROTECTION' French assets were underperforming broader European markets on Monday, though moves were more contained than at some other moments of recent political friction. Tensions in President Emmanuel Macron's fragile government over apparent security shortcomings — coming as the government needs to pass a budget bill to rein in its finances — could further unsettle investors. Macron's office said on Monday he had turned down his Interior Minister Laurent Nunez's offer to resign, telling him instead to put an end to barricades and looting and be transparent over what Macron called "intelligence and foresight failings". Nunez told reporters that Tuesday evening's Champions League soccer match between Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona would go ahead as planned. The mayors of Paris, Marseille and Lyon said in a joint op-ed in the newspaper Liberation that they were used to demonstrations and protests. "But on Saturday ... ‌for the first time, we had the feeling that whole sections of our cities had been left without protection," said the ​mayors, all from the centre-left. The start of school holidays on Monday may provide relief, but students were staging more gatherings and blockades in some places, ​including the Louvre gallery and Sciences Po university in central Paris. LUXURY BOUTIQUES DAMAGED At the weekend, hundreds of thousands ​took to the streets to protest over what many say are declining and dysfunctional public services. At the Place Vendome in Paris, home to luxury hotels and boutiques, most shops were shuttered ‌and surrounded by security guards on Monday. The front door of a Dior boutique was ​smashed, while windows belonging to other luxury brand stores in ​central Paris, including Rolex, Louis Vuitton, Ralph Lauren and Gucci, were damaged. In Marseille, Ligue 1 club Olympique de Marseille said its official store on the city's historic main avenue had been looted, while a town hall in central France was torched. France deployed 60,000 police and other security forces on Saturday, Nunez told France Inter radio, but he acknowledged that was not enough to control violent crowds. Cost-of-living issues also drove ​weekend protests in other European countries including Italy, Belgium and Albania. European governments have ‌advised citizens travelling to France to avoid large crowds and exercise caution. As France was busy cleaning up its streets, Macron arrived in Kuwait for a Gulf trip aimed at securing additional petrol ​and diesel supplies to bring down pump prices. (Reporting by Zhifan Liu, Tassilo Hummel, Elizabeth Pineau, Dominique Vidalon, Alessandro Parodi and Makini Brice in Paris, Sudip Kar-Gupta in Brussels, Amanda Cooper, Alun John ​and Helen Reid in London; Writing by Tassilo Hummel and Charlie Devereux; Editing by Aidan Lewis and Andrew Cawthorne) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/world/articles/frances-macron-declines-interior-ministers-052023968.html

articles.title: West Virginia officials offered to store nuclear waste. Then residents found out.
articles.summary: HARPERS FERRY, W.Va. - The jagged limestone rocks of Old Standard Quarry have weathered many eras of history. The property was the site of a Civil War battle, then a quarry and is now a popular destination for bungee jumping, its dark green water fed by a natural spring. Recently, the state proposed yet another use for the land: as storage for radioactive nuclear waste from around the country. Subscribe to The Post Most newsletter for the most important and interesting stories from The Washington Post. “I thought it was a joke,” said Pasha Majdi, president of the Jefferson County Commission. “It doesn’t make any sense.” It wasn’t a joke. Without consulting residents or local officials, Gov. Patrick Morrisey’s energy office submitted a detailed pitch to the Trump administration offering the Jefferson County quarry and three other sites for a potential “Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campus.” The Trump administration has said such campuses would need to agree to store spent nuclear fuel - one of the nation’s most vexing environmental problems - in exchange for federal support for research, development and production facilities that aim to modernize and grow the country’s nuclear power infrastructure. The administration claims the campuses could create 25,000 jobs and generate tens of billions of dollars in private investment and tax revenue. Those economics are alluring to states eager for development. Twenty-six expressed some manner of interest before the federal government chose Utah, Tennessee, Oklahoma, Louisiana, Idaho and West Virginia as finalists. “West Virginia is intentionally beginning with nuclear initiatives that are actionable and high‑value, particularly those tied to the spent and partially spent fuel stream and backend services, areas where the state can quickly demonstrate success and build momentum,” the state’s pitch promised. It assured that “West Virginia recognizes that for any project with potential community impacts, social buy-in and community alignment are foundational.” But the way things played out in West Virginia underscored how community anxiety around nuclear waste is not easily overcome. That anxiety is why there is no comprehensive plan for permanently disposing of the tens of thousands of tons of spent fuel that already exists in the United States, much less for getting rid of the waste that could be generated with the quadrupling of nuclear power capacity President Donald Trump envisions. As soon as details of the West Virginia proposal were disclosed, thanks to a public records request by the Charleston Gazette-Mail, the backlash was intense. Days after dismissing the report as “fake news,” Morrisey (R) withdrew the state from consideration altogether. The Morrisey administration did not respond to requests for comment. Energy Department spokesman Ben Dietderich said in an emailed statement that “the program has proven to be a huge success - with more than 25 states applying to participate - much of that success can be attributed [to] allowing states and local communities decide for themselves if an innovation campus is right for them.” The West Virginia episode, though, left communities bewildered, the governor politically wounded and the nuclear waste problem unresolved. The nuclear life cycle campus competition comes after the federal government tried - and failed - to create a repository for spent fuel for decades. Congress had designated Yucca Mountain, Nevada, as the most suitable place for it. But local opposition derailed that plan. Now, the focus is on finding a “consent-based” solution that would be developed in coordination with communities interested in developing facilities. Such a model has been successful in parts of Europe. It typically takes many years of deliberation and negotiation by the communities involved. “I’m personally a bit skeptical that states are going to move as fast as the [Trump] administration wants or is expecting,” said Matt Bowen, a nuclear scholar at Columbia University’s Center on Global Energy Policy who has been tracking the life cycle campus initiative. The difficult conversations state officials need to have with the cities and counties that would host nuclear campuses are just getting underway. Nuclear industry officials say states taking a deliberative, democratic approach are getting genuine interest from communities that are viable candidates for a campus. In West Virginia, though, state officials appear not to have communicated with each other or the towns they were offering up in their pitch. And their experience shows how quickly the process can go sideways. Far from the fast-growing Harpers Ferry region, in economically struggling Boone County, the state’s nuclear pitch called for storing waste at what was once one of the largest mountaintop-removal coal mines in the country - an environmentally damaged site the state and local community have for years been seeking to convert into a redevelopment opportunity. The former coal-mining stronghold has lost nearly one-fifth of its population since 2010, as jobs disappeared. But the nuclear campus proposal landed with a thud there, too. Local opposition quickly emerged. The area’s state representative expressed frustration on social media that the community had not been consulted and relief when the state scrapped the proposal. The proposal had highlighted the potential benefits of a new state law, written for data center developers, that allows for fast-track approval of permits while bypassing local governments. “It felt for many of us like: ‘Here we go again,’” said Christine Wimer, president of the Jefferson County Foundation, a conservation advocacy group. “This is the same old thing in West Virginia. People come here. They get the good stuff. We get taken advantage of.’” Wimer said everything about the site the state was proposing near Harpers Ferry was unworkable. The porous limestone is particularly ill-suited for storing toxic materials. Half the property is a federally protected conservation zone, forever honoring its status as a historic battlefield. The other half, she said, is underwater. “Limestone essentially works like a highway for waste,” said Cara Keys, a county commissioner, as she stood over the quarry. “You could put something here, and it could infect someone’s well 20 miles away. The fact that they thought this could be a nuclear waste dump is very concerning.” Steve Pearson, editor of Jefferson County’s Observer Weekly newspaper, dove deep into the details of the proposal and emerged perplexed how it ever got submitted. “Even if you just wanted to build a warehouse, you could not do it there,” he said. “There is no land for it.” Down the road from the quarry in Middleway, a remarkably well-preserved village of 18th- and 19th-century stone, brick and log buildings on the National Register of Historic Places, farmers were already exhausted trying to stop plans for a large water-bottling plant that developers are seeking to build over the vociferous objections of community leaders, who warn it would be an environmental mess. The news that the state hoped to store nuclear waste nearby left them stunned. “I like to be left alone,” said David Liskey, 75, who has been in the area all his life. His ancestors started farming there in the mid-1700s. “People like it here the way it is. We don’t want what they are talking about doing.” Gabby Wilson has only been in the area a short time, having recently relocated from North Carolina. But Wilson, the owner of Prismatic Art Studio in downtown Charles Town, was every bit as blunt as Liskey. “It’s just gross,” she said of the nuclear campus proposal. “We moved here to get away from things like that.” Related Content This article originally appeared on Washington Post at https://washingtonpost.com/business/2026/10/19/how-pitch-store-nuclear-waste-by-historic-battlefield-fell-apart/

articles.title: Mass. GOP candidate for lieutenant governor suspends campaign after arrest
articles.summary: The former Massachusetts lieutenant governor-hopeful who was arrested in connection with drunken driving on Saturday night appeared in New Bedford court on Monday morning. Shawn Oliver, 42, is facing charges of operating under the influence (OUI) of alcohol in addition to motor vehicles charges of negligent operation, marked lanes violation and speeding, according to charging documents in his case. Oliver pleaded not guilty and was ordered released on personal recognizance from New Bedford District Court on Monday morning by Judge Joseph Harrington Jr. He is scheduled to appear again on Nov. 16. Oliver is a current New Bedford city councilor and Bristol County House of Corrections officer who was running on the ticket as a Republican candidate with Mike Minogue against current Lt. Gov. Kim Driscoll and Gov. Maura Healey. He announced he was suspending his campaign at around 2 p.m. on Sunday, less than 24 hours after his arrest Saturday night and after Minogue had called on him to do so Sunday morning. Read more: The Mass. GOP’s lieutenant governor candidate suspended his campaign. Here’s what’s next “After careful reflection, I have made the decision to suspend my campaign for Lieutenant Governor,” Oliver, who was running as a Republican in the race, said in a statement released at 2:17 p.m. on Sunday. “This election is too important to be overshadowed by personal matters. I want to sincerely thank everyone who has supported me throughout this journey and ask that my family’s privacy be respected during this difficult time,” Oliver said. Oliver’s attorney could not immediately be reached for comment Monday. What happened? According to three New Bedford police reports on the incident, Oliver was driving a black Lincoln Navigator north on Dartmouth Street at around 11:30 p.m., just south of the Rockdale Avenue intersection. A witness who spoke to officers at the scene said he was stopped in his own car behind Oliver’s Navigator at an intersection light on Dartmouth Street. When the light turned green, the witness said the Navigator did not pull forward. After a few moments sitting at the light — and the witness reversing his own car to view that the light was green — the Navigator suddenly accelerated forward and drifted to the right, almost hitting the curb by New York Bagel at 571 Dartmouth St., the report read. The Navigator then “abruptly” veered to the left to avoid striking the curb, the report read, and continued onward. After crossing through the Dartmouth and Rockdale intersection, the Navigator again drifted to the left and crossed over the yellow center line. Police say Oliver struck five parked cars and was driving so fast that he flipped his Navigator upside down onto its roof. Oliver was outside of the car and standing on the sidewalk, speaking on his cellphone when officers arrived at the scene, the report read. A bystander brought out a chair and officers told Oliver to sit down, noting that he was bleeding from an injury on the right side of his head. Oliver repeatedly asked officers at the scene if “everyone else was OK,” though they told him he was the only person involved in the crash, the report read. Oliver also told officers he was “burning both ends of the wick,” and said he “was coming from a meeting with friends in Dartmouth.” Oliver was unable to complete a field sobriety test due to his injuries and was brought to the hospital, where he then told officers he’d drank at least two alcoholic beverages earlier in the night at Black Bass Grill. He then had gone to a friend’s house located in Dartmouth, police said. Oliver’s eyes were “bloodshot and glassy,” he was emanating “a moderate odor of alcoholic beverages” and he vomited at the hospital before he was placed under arrest. “After speaking with Shawn, it was determined that he was under the influence of alcoholic beverages therefore should not have been operating a motor vehicle,” the report read. “At this point he was advised that he was being placed under arrest and was handcuffed to the hospital bed,” the report read. Oliver refused to have his blood drawn at the hospital. articles.title: 11 missing after boat capsizes off Mexico, with survivors showing signs of shark bites
articles.summary: The U.S. Coast Guard has suspended its search to find 11 people estimated missing after a boat carrying 27 people capsized Friday in the Pacific Ocean. The search was halted Sunday evening after the Coast Guard, alongside Mexican authorities and the U.S. Navy, searched more than 2,441 square miles for a combined 89 hours, the Coast Guard said. "We are grateful for the exceptional coordination and assistance from Mexico and the U.S. Navy throughout this challenging operation," said Capt. Joseph Meuse, chief of staff, Coast Guard Southwest District said in the statement Monday. "Suspending a search is never easy, and this was an exceptionally dynamic case, far offshore, in rough weather. We can say with confidence that human traffickers have zero regard for human life and routinely put the lives of illegal aliens and the lives of rescue crews at risk." Aircraft and vessels spent the weekend searching for the missing passengers in waters about 140 miles west of Ensenada, Mexico, after the U.S. Coast Guard received multiple distress calls around 1 a.m. Friday, reporting a vessel taking on water. Helicopter crews arrived about an hour later and found passengers floating amid debris. It took around 90 minutes to pull 16 people from the water. Three of the 16 survivors pulled from the water were treated for injuries consistent with shark bites, Petty Officer Charlie Valor told The New York Times on Sunday. "People were holding onto each other, to debris, just treading and trying to stay above water before being rescued," Lt. Santiago Tamburini told CBC over the weekend. All 16 survivors are Mexican nationals, the Mexican consulate in San Diego told the Associated Press . The survivors were taken to a Coast Guard base in San Diego and then to local hospitals, where two are in critical condition, CBC reported. The boat's point of departure and destination remain unclear, as does the purpose of the voyage. The Coast Guard has described the vessel as following a route normally used in illegal maritime smuggling operations, and Meuse said in Monday's statement that human traffickers "routinely put the lives" of people and rescue crews at risk. "Boats in that area can be for fishing, leisure or personal recreation. We just don't know what they were doing out there. We all know it's a suspected smuggling route," Tamburini said. Capt. Robert Tucker said in a statement that the case "highlights the extreme dangers of taking to the sea." "The vessel had a large number of people onboard and was following a route normally used in illegal maritime smuggling operations. Offshore conditions are unforgivable and can quickly result in death," he added. On Sunday, the agency confirmed that Homeland Security Investigations will lead an inquiry into the incident. U.S. Customs and Border Protection is interviewing the survivors, the Coast Guard said. articles.title: Mike Johnson raises concerns over Trump's Russia sanctions waiver as GOP criticism grows
articles.summary: Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) said Sunday that he warned the White House of “unintended consequences” that could stem from waiving sanctions on Russia . President Trump signed an executive order last week waiving sanctions on Russia that were slated to take effect under a legislative package championed by former Sen. Lindsey Graham (R-S.C.) and passed by Congress with overwhelming bipartisan support. The move quickly sparked bipartisan backlash. Asked whether he wants to waive the tariffs or forgo the move, Johnson told Fox News host Larry Kudlow, “Congress voted on this decisively just several weeks ago, and we understand that Putin cannot be trusted.” “He demonstrates that over and over and over,” Johnson said. “So I did talk to several of my colleagues yesterday who had concerns about that. They're on committees of jurisdiction, like intelligence and foreign affairs, and I didn't talk to the president yesterday because he and I are both traveling nonstop and we’re on different schedules. But I told the White House team that we need to talk about it, and I think carefully consider the unintended consequences that may ensue from that.” Johnson added that he knows the “president's evaluating this as he does everything else.” “Look, he has two major objectives, as you know, Larry. Every day he wants to keep America safe, and he wants to bring down the cost of living for every American. He thinks outside the box with creative ideas all the time, and he carefully evaluates those. So I think the right decision will be made here in the end,” Johnson said. Several GOP lawmakers, meanwhile, were quick to bash Trump’s move. “What part of enforcing a law passed 86-11 by the Senate does the President and his advisors not understand? It’s unconscionable that this administration is capitulating to a Russian dictator who illegally invaded Ukraine and butchers innocent civilians every single day,” Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N.C.) wrote on the social platform X. Rep. Don Bacon (R-Neb.) wrote on X that the president is “prolonging the war, not ending it.” Trump has defended the move, writing in a Truth Social post that he is “in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine, and don’t want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table.” Copyright 2026 Nexstar Media, Inc. articles.title: Ukraine claims world's first drone evacuation of wounded soldier
articles.summary: Ukraine's 92nd Separate Assault Brigade shared a video on Monday showing an injured soldier evacuated by drone. (Ukraine's 92nd Assault Brigade) Ukraine has shared a video showing what it says is the world’s first evacuation of an injured soldier from the frontlines by drone. The “historic” mission comes just as Kyiv faces a dire turn in its relationship with Washington over the withdrawal of support in its fight against Russia . Shared by the 92nd Separate Assault Brigade on Monday, the video shows the soldier strapping himself into a large drone and being flown at what appears to be relatively low altitude over blurred-out territory. The drone carefully lowers him down and the drone operator greets him with “Welcome back to the ground!” The video also showed blurred faces of drone operators who carried out the mission. The post said the unidentified infantryman was wounded while at his position. “Due to intense enemy drone activity and the presence of landmines, evacuation using conventional unmanned ground vehicles was impossible,” the brigade said. “At that point, the specialists in our unit took it upon themselves to attempt something that had never been done before: evacuating a serviceman using an aerial drone,” it added. The craft used was a heavy-lift hexacopter, it said, originally designed as a bomber by a Ukrainian manufacturer. It looks about twice the size of the soldier in the video. The specialists working on the mission had to ensure the drone could carry a human being without flipping over or swaying excessively, according to the unit. The rescued soldier is currently undergoing treatment and rehabilitation, the brigade added. The squad leader and programmer with the brigade, only identified by his call sign Napalm, called the soldier a “hero” for agreeing to the mission, “having seen and heard the kind of machine that had arrived to get him.” In a separate statement, Ukraine’s Ground Forces said its drone units are already conducting operations “that were recently considered science fiction.” The unidentified infantryman was lifted out in a drone rescue mission after he was wounded at his position. (Ukraine's 92nd Separate Assault Brigade ) The war has increasingly become a technological arms race, with both Ukraine and Russia relying on drones to reduce human casualties. The conflict has taken a severe toll on both armies, although neither side reports up-to-date numbers of those killed, injured or missing. Ukraine in particular has faced a severe shortage of manpower as it has tried to ramp up recruitment. Ukraine had a major leap in drone technology this year, allowing it to limit Russian logistics in occupied territories as well as strike deeper inside Russia to target Russian oil refineries , commercial warehouses and data centers . Fires at an oil refinery in Moscow, following a reported Ukrainian drone strike, on Sept. 20. (Reuters) “This mission proves once again that Ukrainian service members, working in tandem with Ukrainian manufacturers, are setting global trends in the conduct of warfare,” the brigade’s statement added. Despite hoping that its drone innovation would give it the upper hand at the negotiating table, Kyiv has faced pressure from the U.S. to halt its strikes on Russian oil sites after President Donald Trump signed a diesel deal with the Kremlin earlier this month. Kyiv has since also reported gaps in intelligence sharing and restrictions on Elon Musk’s Starlink service that is crucial for its drone missions, battlefield communications and air defense. A Russian missile strike on an apartment building in Kyiv on Tuesday. (Genya Savilov/AFP; Yan Dobronosov/Global Images Ukraine / via Getty) The drone evacuation comes just days after Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi announced the Ukrainian government had approved an “experimental project” to use drones for medical logistics. Koretskyi said flights would require coordination with the military, and drones would be given a special status and would be identifiable in the air. “During the war, moving medical cargo by road can cost critical time, especially for transplants,” he said. “Drones will be able to carry medicines, medical products, blood samples, and donor organs between hospitals, including from remote areas.” This article was originally published on NBCNews.com This article originally appeared on NBC News at https://www.nbcnews.com/world/ukraine/ukraine-first-drone-evacuation-wounded-soldier-frontlines-hexacopter-rcna604310

articles.title: Falling crucifix kills Ecuador priest during livestreamed church service
articles.summary: A Catholic priest in Ecuador has died after he was fatally crushed by a falling crucifix while live-streaming evening mass. The shocking accident occurred on Saturday at the Nuestra Senora del Perpetuo Socorro Church in Guayaquil, Ecuador's largest city, some 265km southwest of the capital. Patricio Alfredo Sánchez Molinari was broadcasting the event live from his social media accounts when the mounted cross on the wall behind him fell suddenly, around 30 minutes into the stream. Graphic footage of the mass showed a heavy crucifix hanging behind the altar detaching and falling onto the back of the priest’s head. Patricio Sánchez Molinari was killed by a cross while live streaming Catholic Mass (Facebook /  Patricio Sánchez) The priest was facing the congregation at the time and did not appear to see it fall. The video showed he did not stand up again after being struck. The priest was knocked below the altar and out of view, but recorded horrified worshippers shouting out and rushing to his aid. “Father, Father! Call an ambulance!” people could be heard shouting just before the broadcast cut out. Others could be seen rushing towards the altar to help the stricken cleric. Emergency services were immediately called to the scene, but first responders were unable to revive the priest. The video of the livestream was later taken down from the priest’s page, but circulated widely on social media, NBC News reported. The archdiocese of Guayaquil confirmed his death on Sunday, writing that Sanchez “has left to the House of the Father to enjoy his presence and glory”. The priest was hosting evening mass when he was hit by the cross on the wall behind him (Facebook / Patricio Sanchez) “Eternal rest grant unto him, O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon him. May he rest in peace. Amen,” they wrote in a statement in Latin published on social media. The archdiocese did not say what had caused the crucifix to fall or whether there would be an investigation. It was unclear whether he was killed instantly or died later from injuries. Sánchez belonged to the Congregation of the Most Holy Redeemer, a Roman Catholic religious order founded in 1732 with a presence in 80 countries, according to the Associated Press. A Eucharist in his memory was scheduled for Sunday evening, the archdiocese said. Local authorities were yet to comment on the incident, and it was not clear what caused the crucifix to fall. In 2014, a 21-year old man died and his friend was injured after they were crushed by a crucifix erected in honour of Pope John Paul II in northern Italy . The same year, a mother of two died in Chicago, US, after a stone gargoyle fell three stories from an old church, striking her as she was taking a walk with her fiancé. articles.title: DOJ accuses judge in D.C. golf course case of violating 'basic norms' of impartiality
articles.summary: A federal judge refused the Department of Justice's (DOJ) demand to step aside from a key hearing on Monday over the future of East Potomac Park, which President Trump wants to renovate into a championship-style golf course. The Trump administration has accused U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes of bias after she yelled at a government attorney last week to express disappointment that hundreds of trees were cut down at the park without additional notice. The DOJ accused her of “violating the basic norms” that a judge be fair and impartial. “It is easy to weaponize selective quotations to bring a baseless recusal motion. But it is much harder to meet the demanding legal standard against a full record,” Reyes wrote in a 13-page opinion denying the effort late Sunday. “By any objective measure, the Government fails to meet the standard for recusal,” she continued. Reyes, an appointee of former President Biden who serves on the federal bench in the nation’s capital, oversees a lawsuit brought by a preservationist group and individual golfers. They challenge Trump’s desire for a massive renovation at East Potomac Park that would shift it into a championship-style golf course, saying the project is unlawful. The president unveiled a new plan for the site Sunday. “The judge on the case is a crazed lunatic whose courthouse tapes will reveal, may be insane?” Trump wrote on Truth Social early Monday. The lawsuit has been ongoing for months, but tensions reached a new high after the administration informed the judge on a Friday afternoon that hundreds of trees would be cut down that weekend. The judge has said she’s furious and disappointed with the government for not providing her additional notice before the landscaping, and she has since blocked any additional tree-clearing. The Justice Department in demanding her recusal took issue with the judge’s heated rhetoric — at one point she asked a government lawyer if they were unable to use a phone or drive a car — as well as her demands that Trump administration witnesses show up on a federal holiday to testify before her. “The Government created an emergent situation. articles.title: 沙特"沙漠达沃斯"推迟至2027年：500亿美元签约窗口关闭，"全球商业枢纽"叙事受挫
articles.summary: 沙特阿拉伯旗舰投资会议"未来投资倡议"（FII）宣布推迟举行，中东安全局势的持续恶化令这一被称为"沙漠达沃斯"的全球金融盛会无法如期落地，沙特将自身打造为全球商业枢纽的雄心由此蒙上阴影。 10月19日，主办方发表声明， 确认原定于10月26日至29日在利雅得举行的第十届FII大会将延至2027年举行，并表示将"很快"公布新的具体日期。 声明称，此次推迟是为了确保这一"重要里程碑活动能够达到合作伙伴、会员、演讲嘉宾和参会代表所期待的规模、质量和影响力"。 此次推迟发生在胡塞武装对沙特境内目标发动一系列袭击之后。10月10日，胡塞武装袭击利雅得哈立德国王国际机场，造成至少12至18人死亡、300多人受伤。 此后，胡塞武装持续对沙特发动导弹和无人机袭击，波及军事、能源及民用基础设施，包括沙特国家石油公司沙特阿美总部。 金融界巨头原定与会，安全顾虑迫使计划搁浅 本届"未来投资倡议"大会原本汇聚了一份星光熠熠的嘉宾名单。 据草案议程，原定出席者包括高盛首席执行官David Solomon、渣打银行首席执行官Bill Winters、花旗集团首席执行官Jane Fraser，以及摩根大通首席执行官杰米·戴蒙、黑石集团首席执行官史蒂芬·施瓦茨曼、贝莱德首席执行官拉里·芬克等金融界重量级人士。 据路透报道，多家大型银行和私募股权机构已私下向沙特公共投资基金（PIF）总裁亚西尔·鲁迈扬转达了对参会安全性的担忧。 据悉，部分参会者和演讲嘉宾原计划先乘飞机抵达巴林，再驱车约5小时前往利雅得，以规避直飞风险。 主办方此前亦曾考虑采取混合线上参会等应急方案，就在上周还表示正为"迎接数千名代表来到利雅得"作准备，但最终仍不得不宣布推迟。 "未来投资倡议"八年积累成果丰厚，推迟打击沙特经济转型战略 "未来投资倡议"由沙特主权财富基金于2017年创立，已成长为沙特推动经济多元化、吸引外资的核心平台。 首届大会期间，沙特王储穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼在此公布了规模宏大的NEOM新未来城超级项目。 鲁迈扬曾表示，自该倡议创立以来，FII促成的交易累计超过2500亿美元，其中仅2025年一届便达成逾500亿美元协议。 此次停办，对沙特而言代价不小。沙特正大力推进价值数万亿美元的经济转型计划，致力于降低对石油的依赖，向旅游、体育和科技等领域拓展，亟需持续吸引全球资本的关注与投入。 此次推迟折射出美伊战争向中东地区蔓延所带来的更广泛冲击。 据路透报道，今年以来，阿联酋和卡塔尔已有多场会议因安全局势相继取消、推迟或调整形式。沙特此前受冲击相对较小，但近期随着胡塞武装袭击强度升级，形势明显趋紧。 "未来投资倡议"推迟举行，是海湾地区商务活动因地缘政治风险而受阻的最新案例，也再度提示市场：中东安全局势的演变，正成为影响该地区商业环境与投资者信心的重要变量。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 惠誉点名美国主权评级下调风险，发达市场债务利息突破3.3万亿美元
articles.summary: 在2026财年美国联邦赤字扩大至1.99万亿美元、净利息支出达到创纪录的1.05万亿美元的背景下，惠誉评级明确点名美国主权评级面临下调风险。 美国财政部10月16日公布的数据显示，截至9月30日的2026财年，美国联邦政府财政赤字达到1.99万亿美元，同比扩大约12%，为2021年以来最大年度财政赤字，连续第四年维持在这一高位水平。 美国国债收益率上升使利息支出飙升，成为推动财政赤字扩大的关键因素。2026财年，美国联邦政府净利息支出同比增加814亿美元，达到创纪录的1.05万亿美元，成为政府三大支出项目之一。 惠誉预计，到年底发达市场政府债务总额将突破75万亿美元； 据国际金融协会（IIF）数据，即便在本轮债券抛售潮之前，富裕国家政府每年支付的利息已超过3.3万亿美元，超过全球国防开支或人工智能投资总额。 惠誉将美国、法国、英国列为债务稳定面临威胁、主权评级面临下调风险的国家，并明确：若高额财政赤字、利息支出占财政收入比重、政府债务占GDP比重三项指标持续恶化，且缺乏可信的中期财政调整方案，美国主权评级将面临下调压力。 政府发债与科技巨头融资形成双重挤压 惠誉评级首席经济师Brian Coulton将本轮债市收益率飙升归因于供需两端的共同作用。 他指出： 能源冲击持续时间超出此前预期，改变了市场对货币政策的判断，也让各国央行更加警惕通胀的第二轮效应。 值得关注的是，不仅中短期债券承压，30年期超长期国债收益率也在同步攀升，而中长期通胀预期基本保持稳定。Brian Coulton表示： 这说明更广泛的供需因素同样在发挥作用。 供给端压力首先来自各国政府持续扩大的财政赤字。 国际货币基金组织10月在最新《世界经济展望》中指出，全球发达经济体今年净借款规模将达GDP的5.2%，创2021年以来新高。 美国财政部数据显示，截至9月30日的2026财年，美国联邦政府财政赤字达1.99万亿美元，同比扩大约12%，为2021年以来最大年度赤字，连续第四年维持高位；净利息支出同比增加814亿美元，达创纪录的1.05万亿美元，成为政府三大支出项目之一。 与此同时，科技巨头的大规模融资正与主权债券争夺市场资金。 Brian Coulton指出： 在AI投资热潮下，大型科技云企业开始大举融资，以支持数据中心和IT基础设施建设，在债务市场与主权债券形成资金竞争。 高盛曾预计，五大超大规模云服务商，谷歌、亚马逊、Meta、微软和甲骨文在2026年发债规模约为2500亿美元，2027年将进一步升至4000亿美元。Brian Coulton总结称： 在投资需求上升、储蓄并未同步增长的背景下，这给美国以及全球实际利率带来上行压力。 美法英承压最重，债务期限结构成关键变量 惠誉评级西欧主权评级主管、高级董事Federico Barriga-Salazar认为， 融资成本上升对所有发达市场均构成压力，尤其是债务高企且债券集中到期规模较大的国家，法国、美国和英国首当其冲。 IMF总裁格奥尔基耶娃近日警告，发达经济体已成为债务问题上"最严重的违规者"。 随着偿债利息持续攀升，各国财政空间被进一步压缩，为民众提供生活成本支持的能力也将受到限制。 一国财政抵御冲击的能力，在很大程度上取决于存量债务的平均剩余期限。 Federico Barriga-Salazar指出，英国政府债务平均剩余期限为13.4年，法国为8.2年，这意味着债券收益率飙升向整体财政利率负担的传导将是渐进的。 然而，他同时警告，法国短期到期债务规模占GDP的15.9%，一旦市场融资条件恶化，将对法国财政产生短期流动性冲击。 针对外界对法国债市动荡可能重燃欧债危机的担忧，Federico Barriga-Salazar给出了相对审慎的评估。他强调，欧洲已在制度层面构筑多重防线，包括欧洲稳定机制（ESM）、银行业联盟以及欧洲央行的各类支持工具，其核心正是为了遏制风险溢出效应演化为系统性危机。 三大指标恶化或触发主权评级下调 惠誉评级主权及超国家机构研究全球主管、董事总经理Ed Parker明确列出了触发主权评级下调的关键信号： 高额财政赤字能否收窄、利息支出占财政收入的比率是否持续走高，以及政府债务占GDP的比率能否企稳。 他警告： 如果这几项指标持续恶化，而政府又拿不出可信的中期财政调整方案，就可能对主权评级形成下调压力。 惠誉报告显示，全球十大发达经济体10年期国债收益率中位数，比未偿债务的平均利率高出161个基点，这使得降低甚至稳定债务水平变得愈发困难。 Ed Parker指出，政府债券普遍期限较长，债券收益率上行需要一段时间才会传导至存量债务的平均有效利率，这给政府留出了一定调整窗口。但他同时强调： 若债务/GDP比快速攀升，同时缺乏可信的财政方案、也不具备落实政策的政治执行力，就意味着公共债务可持续性风险上升。 以法国为例，惠誉测算显示，若要让债务负担保持稳定，其基本财政赤字需从今年预期的2.9%降至GDP的0.4%；若实际融资成本上行至当前市场收益率水平，法国还需额外实施规模约相当于GDP的3.1%的财政调整。 Ed articles.title: 伊朗警告美国：即便“有限度”重启轰炸，“世界也将面临严重能源危机”
articles.summary: 伊朗军事与外交官员密集发出战事升级警告，将美国潜在恢复轰炸行动与全球能源供应中断直接挂钩，令市场对霍尔木兹海峡通道安全的担忧骤然升温。在两艘油轮于该海峡遭袭起火后，能源市场正面临重新评估供应中断风险定价是否充分的压力。 伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队（IRGC）发言人Hossein Mohebbi于当地时间19日周一明确表示：“即便美国的行动是有限的，世界也将面临严重的能源危机。” 这是迄今为止伊朗官员将军事冲突与能源市场冲击最为直接挂钩的表态之一。此前一日，伊朗外长阿拉格齐在社交媒体警告美国总统特朗普，伊朗存在“未完成的任务”，暗示伊方并不排除主动采取进一步行动。 上述警告叠加霍尔木兹海峡油轮遇袭事件，正在从多个维度向能源市场传导压力：原油供应中断预期、航运保险成本攀升，以及地区军事对峙进一步激化的尾部风险。霍尔木兹海峡重开谈判虽仍在进行，但伊朗方面同步释放的强硬信号令谈判前景充满不确定性。 伊朗革命卫队与外长同步发出战事升级警告 Mohebbi在本周一的声明中称，美国在该地区的大多数基地已被迫撤离，其军队“疲惫不堪”，距伊朗数百公里之外，技术和军事上均不具备发动新冲突的能力。 他同时警告，“如果该地区对伊朗变得不安全，整个地区将不再有安全可言”，并强调伊朗的回应“这一次将远比此前严厉”。 阿拉格齐上周日在社交媒体发文，以更具挑衅性的语气回应特朗普关于恢复轰炸的表态：“上次你们想'完成任务'，伊朗变得更强大了。想再试试运气？请便。但要小心，我们也有未完成的任务。” 他还将以色列总理内塔尼亚胡描述为将美国拖入新战争的推手，并将其动机与即将到来的以色列选举及个人司法困境相挂钩。 伊朗武装力量参谋长、少将Ali Abdollahi亦于周日发出警告，称德黑兰已在数月的美国打击中“屹立不倒”，任何进一步攻击都将遭到“更具侵略性的报复”。 霍尔木兹油轮遇袭，能源市场定价面临考验 上述密集警告的直接背景，是伊朗革命卫队宣称在霍尔木兹海峡击中两艘试图通过"未经授权"航线的油轮，称船只在触雷后起火。这是近期该海峡发生的最新一起航运安全事件，直接冲击市场对全球约五分之一原油过境通道的安全预期。 Mohebbi关于“即便是有限行动也将引发全球能源危机”的表态，实质上是在向市场发出明确信号：霍尔木兹海峡的封锁或严重干扰并非不可能的极端情景，而是伊朗可动用的现实选项。这一表态对原油价格的风险溢价、航运保险费率以及能源进口国的供应安全评估均构成直接压力。 目前，能源市场面临的核心问题在于：此前的定价是否已充分反映霍尔木兹通道中断的概率。油轮遇袭事件发生后，航运保险成本已出现上行，但分析人士需要评估的是，伊朗将军事升级与能源危机明确挂钩的最新表态，是否代表风险边际的实质性抬升，还是仍属于谈判筹码范畴内的威慑性言辞。 霍尔木兹重开谈判与强硬表态并行 值得关注的是，在强硬军事警告密集释放的同时，外交渠道并未完全关闭。 据央视援引伊朗塔斯尼姆通讯社18日上周日的报道，阿拉格齐在接受媒体采访时表示，伊朗提出的重新开放霍尔木兹海峡的计划仍在谈判桌上。他此前曾表示，伊朗已通过卡塔尔向美国转达相关方案，若美方采取必要行动，霍尔木兹海峡可在七日内恢复正常通行。 与此同时，据报道，巴基斯坦陆军参谋长Asim Munir本周预计将再度访问德黑兰，外界普遍认为此行将传递华盛顿的最新立场，但目前尚不清楚谈判桌上是否仍有实质性提议。 这一"谈判与威慑并行"的双轨态势，令市场难以对局势走向形成清晰预判。伊朗方面一边保留外交出口，一边通过军事官员持续释放升级信号，这种策略性模糊本身即构成市场不确定性的来源之一。 伊朗国内强硬共识趋于巩固 在军事和外交官员发出警告的同时，伊朗国内政治层面的强硬立场也在同步强化。 据新华社，伊朗总统佩泽希齐扬于18日上周日在议会发表讲话，强调伊朗“绝不会屈服于侵略性国家的无理要求和霸凌行径”，并称政府和武装力量正致力于加强国防能力。 新华社提到，伊朗最高国家安全委员会秘书穆赫辛·雷扎伊18日在社交媒体表示，伊朗武装力量已针对任何新的“冒险行径”制定了应对方案，"其破坏力将远超此前"，并强调"伊朗全新的作战计划将不再遵循对方所熟悉的规则"。 新华社还提到，伊朗军队网站18日发布声明回应美方近期发出的所谓使用“炸弹之母”的威胁，称伊朗武装部队已做好充分准备，随时可以应对任何威胁。 以上美方的威胁是指，美国媒体CNN于15日援引多名美国官员的消息报道称，美军方已制定打击伊朗的新方案，其中包括考虑使用有“炸弹之母”之称的大型空爆炸弹打击伊朗核设施。 此外，伊朗最高领袖的顾问Mohammed Mokhber 18日表示，德黑兰的“威慑”已阻止美国和以色列“动用全部能力”，并警告，若美国再度发动攻击，伊朗将寻求将冲突升级为地区性战争。 上述表态显示，伊朗内部在强硬回应问题上已形成高度一致的政治共识，这在一定程度上压缩了伊朗在谈判中作出实质性让步的空间。 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 法国骚乱冲击金融市场：股债双杀，欧元下跌
articles.summary: 法国市场周一遭遇全面抛售。 大规模抗议浪潮 叠加财政整顿前景黯淡，投资者对法国国债风险溢价的担忧急剧升温，债券、股票与欧元同步下挫。 截至发稿，法国10年期国债收益率单日飙升15个基点至4.93%，创近一个月最大单日涨幅，与德国同期国债的利差扩大至146个基点，为两周高位。 CAC 40指数下跌1.5%，法国两大银行法巴银行与兴业银行均跌约3%，领跌欧洲主要市场。欧元兑美元、英镑及日元均下跌0.2%至0.3%。 据新华社周一报道，法国多地日前爆发抗议示威活动，首都巴黎等地出现暴力骚乱。抗议诉求集中于生活成本上涨和公共服务水平下降，凸显法国面临财政危机、福利承压、政治极化等多重矛盾交织的治理困境。 据初步统计，在17日抗议活动期间全法有2000多人被捕，数百家商户遭受严重财产损失。 据彭博，法国中央政府已要求部分地方当局实施宵禁，总理Sebastien Lecornu亦未排除宣布紧急状态的可能性。 财政整顿遭遇政治阻力 此轮动荡的核心，是市场对法国能否有效削减财政赤字的信心动摇。法国经济增长疲软、债务规模持续膨胀，本已承压，而此次社会动乱进一步令预算改革蒙上阴影。 SMBC全球市场策略师Hank Calenti表示："此次市场波动发生在大规模抗议之后，表明改革预期正在减退。"他所指的改革，涵盖削减财政赤字与推进养老金改革两大议题。 投资者普遍认为，法国须尽快推进预算法案立法，以重建对其财政轨道的信心。然而，明年总统大选前的政治博弈，或将令这一进程更加复杂。 Calenti还指出，此番冲击已波及整个欧元区，多个市场的改革前景均趋于黯淡。值得关注的是，周一德国10年期国债收益率同样上行4个基点至3.45%，而同期美国国债收益率则走低。 法德利差再度走阔，意大利承压 法德10年期国债利差扩至146个基点，为两周内最高水平。尽管较10月初约160个基点的高点有所回落，但市场走势表明，该利差有重返高位的风险。 10月初，法国10年期国债收益率一度触及4.99%，为2002年以来最高水平，而本周收益率正再度逼近这一关键点位。 市场担忧法国债市的波动可能向欧元区其他高负债经济体蔓延，意大利被视为首要观察对象。周一，意大利10年期国债收益率同步上行11个基点至4.58%。 分析人士还指出，对冲基金在法国债市中日益扩大的参与规模，正在加剧市场脆弱性，这一风险已引起监管机构的高度关注。 法国银行股与零售股首当其冲 法国股市成为欧洲主要市场中表现最差的市场，CAC 40指数跌幅达1.5%，高于欧洲斯托克600指数约1%的跌幅。 法国银行股跌幅尤为突出——法巴银行与兴业银行均下挫约3%。历史规律显示，法德利差每度扩大，法国银行股往往率先承压。 零售板块同样未能幸免。家乐福（Carrefour）股价下跌1.8%，其首席执行官表示，公司因抗议破坏蒙受的损失将达数千万欧元。 法国主权信用违约互换（CDS）溢价亦上行5个基点，报约82个基点，虽仍低于10月2日89个基点的阶段高位，但为当日欧洲市场中表现最差的主权CDS。 穆迪将于本周五对法国主权信用评级进行审查，此次审查存在下调评级的可能性，或为法国债市带来额外压力。 不过，德国商业银行（Commerzbank）分析师认为，下调评级对利差的冲击料将有限。"穆迪此举不过是在向其他评级机构靠拢，因此下调评级对利差的负面影响可能相当有限。" 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 美国房屋建筑商信心超预期跌至14年低点，高利率与成本压力双重夹击
articles.summary: 美国房屋建筑市场持续承压，行业信心加速滑落至逾十年最低水平。 全美房屋建筑商协会（NAHB）与富国银行联合发布的 住房市场景气指数本月下滑3点至29，为2012年6月以来最低，低于彭博调查经济学家预期中值31 。该指数连续逾两年低于荣枯分水岭50，显示认为市场状况不佳的建筑商持续占多数。 抵押贷款利率处于7%以上的高位、劳动力短缺以及建筑成本居高不下，令建筑商承压加剧。NAHB首席经济学家Robert Dietz表示： "住房市场仍受制于供给侧约束与严峻的可负担性挑战，更高的抵押贷款利率、高昂的建筑成本以及消费者信心走弱，令更多潜在买家持观望态度。" 市场对该行业前景保持悲观。追踪房屋建筑商及建材企业的iShares美国房屋建筑ETF过去三个月持续下跌。 核心分项指标全线走弱，激励措施使用比例攀升 NAHB报告显示，当前销售分项指数降至33，同为14年最低；未来六个月预期销售指数滑落至2022年11月以来最弱水平；潜在买家流量指数则跌至新冠疫情暴发初期以来最低点。 多项指标同步恶化，折射出建筑商对近期市场走势的普遍悲观预期。借贷成本上升持续抑制购房需求，而新房库存仍处于较高水平，供需两端的双重压力构成明显拖累。 在需求疲软的背景下，建筑商被迫加大促销力度以争取客户。NAHB调查显示， 报告降价的建筑商比例升至43% ，约三分之二的建筑商本月采用了各类激励措施，营业利润率因此承压收窄。 从地区分布来看，南部建筑商信心降至2012年中以来最低，西部信心指数骤降10点，跌至2011年底以来最弱水平；中西部信心亦有所回落，仅东北部出现小幅回升。 美国联邦政府将于周二公布住房开工及建筑许可数据，全美房地产经纪人协会（NAR）亦将发布上月成屋签约销售数据，市场将从中获取住房市场景气状况的进一步信号。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
